title: Magnetic Resonance Elastography Methodology for the Evaluation of Tissue Engineered Construct Growth
protocol: Expand the human mesenchymal stem cells (hMSCs) culture.
Seed hMSCs onto a gelatin sponge at a density of 1x10^6 cells/ml for bone formation or 3x10^6 cells/ml for adipose formation once cells are confluent.

Apply adipose induction media containing 1 μM dexamethasone, 0.5 μM isobutyl-methylxanthine, 10 μg/ml human recombinant-insulin, and 200 μM indomethacin in cell expansion medium once cells appear confluent on the scaffold.
Replace media with 10 μg/ml of human recombinant-insulin in expansion media for 24 hours after three days.
Return to adipose induction media following the insulin incubation period.
Repeat the cycle of changing from induction media to maintenance media and back three times.
Exchange only in maintenance media every two days after completing induction cycles.

Prepare osteogenic induction media by making a final concentration of 0.1 μM dexamethasone, 50 μM L-ascorbic acid-2-phosphate, and 10 mM β-glycerophosphate in cell expansion medium once cells are confluent on the scaffold for bone formation.
Replace osteogenic induction media with fresh media every two days during differentiation.
Apply 0.5% agarose gel at 37°C to enclose the construct in a 10 mm test tube.
Allow the agarose gel five minutes to set at room temperature.
Insert the tip of the piezoelectric bending motor into the surface of the gel.
Attach the tube containing the sample and the actuator to a rigid support.
Orient the beam of the Laser Doppler Vibrometer toward the tip of the mechanical actuator.
Adjust the positioning of the system to optimize the reflected signal, use reflective tape if necessary.
Set the function generator to sweep the desired frequency range (20 to 2000 Hz) using an operating voltage of 20 Vpp with a white noise signal.
View the characterized spectrum on the Polytec Vibrosoft program to identify the resonance frequency of the system.
Set the program to FFT and velocity as the y-axis.
Set the actuator to deliver a continuous sinusoid at the indicated resonance frequency using an operating voltage of 200 Vpp.
Note the generated displacement being delivered to the surface of the gel.
Set Vibrosoft to display the FFT with displacement as the y-axis.
Place the sample and actuator in the center of the MRI scanner.
Use a small RF coil for transmission and reception of the RF signal for tissue construct experiments.
Acquire a scout image for identification of the construct location.
Set the parameters for the acquisition.
Set the repetition time to 1000 ms, echo time to 20-40 ms, slice thickness to 0.5-1.0 mm, and field of view to 12x10 mm² with a matrix size of 128x128 pixels for typical in vitro sagittal scan.
Set the actuator frequency based on Laser Doppler Vibrometer characterization.
Use one bipolar pair with a gradient amplitude of 50 G/cm.
Set the delay to zero milliseconds for initial acquisition.
Change the function generator to burst mode.
Adjust the parameters of the function generator to match those in the elastography acquisition, including frequency and number of cycles.
Set the function generator to be externally triggered.
For a sagittal image, set motion sensitization in the positive slice direction.
Start the scan.
Check the acquired image and change sensitization to negative slice direction.
Execute MATLAB program for complex division to generate shear wave image.
Assess the image for shear waves and artifacts such as phase wrapping.
Adjust parameter array size to eight equally spaced values ranging from zero seconds to a full period of characterized resonance frequency.
Acquire scans in both positive and negative slice orientations.
Use MATLAB program designed for generating shear wave data from an array of images.
Place MRE data into MATLAB program for processing three-dimensional dataset.
Assume planar shear waves to decouple equations of motion.
Estimate complex-valued shear modulus from displacement and its Laplacian.
Approximate spatial second derivatives using finite difference method.
Compute shear modulus on a pixel-by-pixel basis.
Deduce mechanical parameters such as shear wave speed, wave attenuation, shear stiffness, shear elasticity, shear viscosity.
Select regions of interest for calculating mean and standard deviation of each parameter.
Specify imaging parameters at the beginning of the program.
Adjust upper limit of elastogram to optimize sample contrast.
Review intermediate results including filtered waves, temporal FFT, line profiles.
